items.text: $R$ an ordered category (lattice): $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(R,C)$ is preordered, so every functor out of it is faithful — faithfulness of $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(R,C)\to C^I$ is too weak a notion of generation.
$R$ small: algebraic (proved). $R$ large (e.g. the ordinals below the first one not in the universe): not algebraic, though $I=\varnothing$ “generates” it.
Possible condition: the functor $I\to R$ cannot be factored through a proper full $D$-subcategory $R'\subsetneq R$.
Open problem: conditions on $(R,I\to R)$ for the theory to be algebraic with base objects $I$.
Universal problems 1 and 2 known for: finite inverse limits and left exact functors; topoi. To check: additive, abelian, Karoubian categories.
Additive categories as an exactness property
(i) initial and final objects exist and the canonical $\varnothing\to e$ is an isomorphism; (ii) finite sums and products exist, and for two objects:
X\sqcup Y\longrightarrow X\times Y\ \ \text{canonical}\ \ \text{is an isomorphism}
Equivalently every object has a unique monoid and comonoid structure, depending functorially on the object (Eckmann–Hilton).
X\times X\simeq X\sqcup X\to X\ \ \text{(codiagonal: monoid)},\qquad X\to X\sqcup X\simeq X\times X\ \ \text{(diagonal: comonoid)}
Additive = semi-additive + every monoid is a group; “monoid $G$ is a group” $\iff$
G\times G\to G\times G,\quad (x,y)\mapsto(x,xy)\ \ \text{(and its right-hand version) are isomorphisms}
Envelope for finite inverse limits: via the functors $C\to\mathbf{Ab}$ (free abelian group on the representable); the additive case, auto-dual, is not clear.
